thread.title: Charting a jagged June breakout attempt, Nasdaq challenges record territory

author: Michael Ashbaugh
title: Charting a jagged June breakout attempt, Nasdaq challenges record territory
text:
Editor’s Note: This is a free edition of The Technical Indicator, a daily MarketWatch subscriber newsletter. To get this column each market day, click here.
Technically speaking, the major U.S. benchmarks have diverged slightly to start June, though the bigger-picture backdrop remains bullish.
On a headline basis, the Nasdaq Composite is vying for its second straight record close, while the S&P 500 has also broken out, though less decisively, edging to two-month highs.
Before detailing the U.S. markets’ wider view, the S&P 500’s SPX, +0.01% hourly chart highlights the past two weeks.
As illustrated, the S&P has started June on a strong note, clearing resistance matching the May peak (2,742).
The upturn punctuates a fleeting late-May downdraft, fueled by political uncertainty in Italy. Last week’s “Italy-induced” low (2,676) closely matched major support (2,673).
Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average is traversing a jagged near-term range amid technical price action.
Consider that the top of this week’s gap (24,722) has closely matched the 2017 close (24,719).
Conversely, recall that resistance spans from 24,859 to 24,876, a 17-point band matching the April peak and the 2017 peak.
The week-to-date high (24,859) has matched resistance, an area also illustrated on the daily chart.
Against this backdrop, the Nasdaq Composite remains the strongest benchmark.
The index has taken flight to start June, rising to Monday’s record close of 7,606.
Still, the Nasdaq’s absolute record peak — the March peak of 7,637 — rests just overhead, also illustrated below.
Separately, consider that last week’s “Italy-induced” low (7,354) — the Tuesday, May 29 low — closely matched near-term support (7,353). (See the May 22 review. )
Widening the view to six months adds perspective.
On this wider view, the Nasdaq has staged a bull-flag breakout, rising to a record close.
To reiterate, the absolute record peak (7,637.27) — established March 13 — is currently under siege.
The prevailing breakout punctuates a flag pattern underpinned by the 7,320 support, a level closely matching the April peak and the March gap.
Looking elsewhere, the Dow industrials’ backdrop remains comparably softer, but still constructive.
The Dow is the only widely-tracked U.S. benchmark still capped by the April peak (24,859).
This level precisely matched Monday’s session high (24,859) and registers nominally under the 2017 peak (24,876).
More broadly, the prevailing upturn punctuates a successful test of trendline support at last week’s “Italy-induced” low.
Meanwhile, the S&P 500 is acting well technically.
Recall that last week’s low (2,676) registered just above major support at the 2017 close (2,673).
The subsequent rally punctuates a bull flag — pinned to the early-May rally — placing the S&P at two-month highs.
The bigger picture Though the U.S. benchmarks have diverged slightly to start June, the bigger-picture backdrop remains bullish.
On a headline basis, the Nasdaq Composite has tagged a record close, the S&P 500 has reached two-month highs, and the Dow industrials have yet to break out.
Beyond the obvious, each benchmark closely observed support at the ”Italy-induced” late-May low, as detailed above. Constrictive price action.
Moving to the small-caps, the iShares Russell 2000 ETF has extended its break to all-time highs.
The prevailing upturn originates from last week’s low (160.11) punctuating a successful test of the breakout point (160.00) detailed repeatedly.
Technical price action is bullish against the current backdrop.
Meanwhile, the S&P MidCap 400 continues to press a four-month range top.
Resistance broadly spans from about 357.10 to 359.60, and the retest remains underway.
On further strength, the MDY’s record close (362.51) and absolute record peak (363.70) rest within striking distance.
Against this backdrop, the SPDR Trust S&P 500 has reached 10-week highs.
This week’s breakout attempt originates from trendline support closely matching the 2017 peak (268.60).
Summing up the backdrop Collectively, the prevailing technical backdrop is not one-size-fits-all, but on balance, it continues to support a bullish view.
As it applies to the S&P 500, its backdrop has weathered the late-May downdraft.
To reiterate, last week’s low (2,676) closely matched major support (2,673).
The successful retest of support, and subsequent rally to two-month highs, preserves the S&P 500’s recovery attempt.
Additional resistance matches the range top, circa 2,780, while an intermediate-term target projects to the 2,811 area. (Start with the May peak, and subtract the 2017 peak: 2,742 - 2,673 = 69 points. Then, add to the breakout point: 2,742 + 69 = 2,811.)
See also: Charting a slow-motion breakout attempt, Dow 25,000 (still) under siege.
Tuesday’s Watch List The charts below detail names that are technically well positioned. These are radar screen names — sectors or stocks poised to move in the near term. For the original comments on the stocks below, see The Technical Indicator Library.
Drilling down further, the SPDR S&P Biotech ETF XBI, +0.95% has come to life technically.
Specifically, the group has cleared trendline resistance to start June, rising to challenge all-time highs on increased volume.
Underlying the upturn, its relative strength index (not illustrated) has tagged four-month highs, improving the chances of eventual follow-through.
Tactically, the trendline closely matches near-term support, circa 94.50, and a breakout attempt is in play barring a violation.
Looking elsewhere, the Industrial Select Sector SPDR’s XLI, +0.07% backdrop has strengthened in recent weeks. (Yield = 1.6%.)
The group initially spiked two weeks ago, gapping atop a four-month downtrend. The breakout was punctuated by a “higher high” at the May peak, versus the April peak, also consistent with a trend shift.
Tactically, the trendine is closely followed by the 50- and 200-day moving averages, and the group's technical bias points higher barring a violation.
(The XLI’s recent successful test of trendline support dovetails with the Dow industrials’ rally from its trendline, detailed previously.)
Moving to specific names, Twitter, Inc. TWTR, +5.48% is a well positioned large-cap name.
The shares have likely gotten away early Tuesday, rising after S&P Dow Jones Indices announced that Twitter will join the S&P 500 Index, replacing Monsanto, starting Thursday, June 7.
Though near-term extended, the strong-volume spike to three-year highs is longer-term bullish, and the shares are attractive on a pullback. First support matches the breakout point (36.80).
More broadly, Twitter is well positioned on the four-year chart, rising from a jagged continuation pattern pinned to the steep February rally. (And underpinned by February gap support.)
Scientific Games Corp. SGMS, -1.57% is a large-cap developer of technology-based products for the gaming and lottery industries.
The shares initially spiked three weeks ago, reaching record territory after the Supreme Court overturned a federal law that banned sports betting in most locations.
The subsequent flag pattern, also a coiled spring, positions the shares to build on the May spike. Tactically, the post-breakout low (56.80) closely matches major support, and the rally attempt is intact barring a violation.
Kohl’s Corp. KSS, +5.44% is a well positioned large-cap retailer.
As illustrated, the shares have reached three-year highs, clearing well-defined resistance matching the January peak.
The strong-volume breakout comes from a year-to-date range, and an intermediate-term target projects to the 81 area. Conversely, the breakout point (69.50) pivots to first support.
JD.com, Inc. JD, +2.10% is a large-cap Beijing-based e-commerce name.
Technically, the shares have cleared trendline resistance and the 20-day moving average — a widely-tracked near-term trending indicator — rising on increased volume.
The upturn signals a trend shift, originating from major support matching the December low and the May 2017 gap. (See the two-year chart. )
Tactically, gap support (36.40) closely matches the trendline, and the recovery attempt is intact barring a violation.
